S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days of learning of a serious incident involving their model, and promptly provide safety instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, including interim risk controls and a retest schedule. The regulator may restrict or suspend sales if the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk or the manufacturer fails to meet the plan; exceeding 5% alone does not automatically require a sales ban.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For systems already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade plan and complete implementation within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where remote shut-off is not yet available, manufacturers must provide customers with interim emergency guidance.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New battery systems manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying model-specific data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must promptly investigate and determine appropriate protective measures, including recall where warranted by verified incident data, severity, trends, exposure, and corrective actions.

document.section_notes: The 5% figure in S2 is a corrective-action benchmark rather than a hard maximum, and exceeding it never automatically requires a sales stop, which protects the Hearth 10 (6.2%). In S5, the 8-per-100,000 trigger requires notification and a corrective-action plan but makes recall discretionary and open-ended, so a model at 9.9 (Ember 8) is not automatically recalled. S3's 6-year retrofit window and S4's 36-month suppression deadline both sit inside the acceptable ranges, with S4 at the earliest date Halcyon's red line allowed.
